samples.summary: The read boundary this change hardens for `listLevel` still passes `tableData.rowHeights` through a bare `Number(...)`, and an attacker-chosen row height makes the paginator's row-split loop iterate essentially without bound — a persistent hang/OOM for every reader of the document.
samples.evidence: This diff adds `normalizeListLevel` at `treeNodeToBlock` (crdt-tree.ts:249-250) precisely because "a peer's Tree attribute is read straight through `Number(...)`" and every downstream reader multiplies it into geometry. Forty lines above the new clamp, the same function reads row heights with no validation: `attrs.rowHeights.split(',').map(v => (v === '' ? undefined : Number(v)))` (crdt-tree.ts:195-199); the frontend twin does the same at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:453-455. That value is then adopted verbatim as a row minimum — `if (userHeight !== undefined && userHeight > rowHeights[r]) rowHeights[r] = userHeight;` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:245-251), with no ceiling — and reaches the paginator's split loop `while (consumed < rowHeight) { ... consumed += fragHeight; }` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:124-146), where `fragHeight` is capped at one page's `contentHeight` (~900px) and each iteration pushes a `PageLine` and starts a new page. Attack: any principal with write access to the doc — a collaborator on the shared Yorkie tree, or an API key with write scope via `PUT /api/v1/.../content` whose docs validator checks only `Array.isArray(tableData.rows/columnWidths)` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:449-454) — stores `tableData.rowHeights: [1e12]` on one table block. `writeDocsRoot`/`buildBlockNode` serializes it verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:158-162), so it persists; every other client's `paginate()` then loops ~1e9 times allocating pages until the tab dies, and the same code path is used by the PDF export/CLI. Same threat model the diff's own comments invoke ("one hostile collaborator could blank the rendered document ... for every other reader"), reached through the attribute next door instead of `listLevel`. I traced the chain in source but did not execute it, hence medium confidence.

samples.summary: Sibling numeric attributes at the same peer-controlled read boundary (`cell.style.padding`, `colSpan`, `rowSpan`, `cols`) are still coerced with a bare `Number(...)`, so the NaN/absurd-geometry render break the diff eliminates for `listLevel` remains reachable through them.
samples.evidence: `parseCellStyle` does `if (attrs.padding) style.padding = Number(attrs.padding);` (crdt-tree.ts:130 — a non-numeric attribute yields NaN), and `treeNodeToCell` reads `colSpan: attrs.colSpan ? Number(attrs.colSpan) : undefined` / `rowSpan` the same way (crdt-tree.ts:169-170); the frontend store repeats the padding case at yorkie-doc-store.ts:310. Padding flows straight into cell geometry: `const padding = cell?.style?.padding ?? DEFAULT_CELL_PADDING; const innerWidth = Math.max(cellWidth - padding * 2, 0); ... cellHeight = ... + padding * 2` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:188-195). A peer-written `padding` attribute that coerces to NaN yields NaN widths/heights for that cell — exactly the "NaN/Infinity `marginLeft` that blanks the block" failure the diff cites as its reason for clamping the list indent (table-layout.ts:92-97) — and a padding of 1e308 collapses `innerWidth` to 0 while inflating `cellHeight`, feeding the unbounded row height in the finding above. `normalizeTableMerges` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:683) would clamp spans but is only invoked on the clipboard path, not on the CRDT read, so span values are trusted here too (their consumers in table-layout.ts:184/225/268 are bounded, so spans are the least severe of the group).

samples.summary: The docs content-ingest validator enforces finiteness on block *style* numerics but not on `tableData.rowHeights` / `columnWidths` entries, `cell.style.padding`, or `listLevel`, so the API is the durable write path for the poisoned geometry values the client-side clamps now merely tolerate.
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` deliberately rejects a non-finite value for every field in `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` (docs-content.controller.ts:399-407) with the stated doctrine "the geometry fields reach the layout engine as numbers ... hand the caller a 400 instead of silently rewriting their style". The table arm two functions down checks only that `columnWidths` and `rows` are arrays and that each cell has an object `style` (lines 449-484): the numeric *contents* of `columnWidths`/`rowHeights` and `cell.style.padding` are never value-checked, and `listLevel` is not checked anywhere. So an API key with write scope can persist `rowHeights: [1e12]` or `padding: 1e308` and every reader inherits it (see the two findings above); for `listLevel` the new read-boundary clamp means the stored value is merely wrong rather than fatal, but the ingest gate the design note describes as the other half of the invariant ("the backend's content ingest serializes whatever it is handed") is still absent. Low confidence only on whether the maintainers consider ingest validation in scope for this change — the missing checks themselves are verifiable in the cited lines.

Grep colSpan|rowSpan in packages/docs/src/model/types.ts and view/table-layout.ts

samples.summary: `walkCellsForSiblings` recurses through nested table cells with no depth ceiling, so a peer-authored deeply nested table can overflow the stack inside a Tab/Cmd+] gesture.
samples.evidence: The new `walkCellsForSiblings` (document.ts:96-110) recurses per nesting level, and `siblingBlocksOf` calls it as the fallback for every unresolved block (document.ts:325-328). The clipboard parser caps nesting at `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:59), but the CRDT read boundary has no equivalent cap — `treeNodeToBlock`/`treeNodeToCell` recurse unbounded (crdt-tree.ts:151-190) — so nesting depth is attacker-influenced for a client that writes the tree directly. Impact is bounded because the same unbounded recursion already exists on the read itself (and in the pre-existing `walkCellsForBlock`), so this adds a new site rather than new exposure; noted for completeness since the new helper runs synchronously inside a keydown handler, where a throw abandons the gesture mid-write.

verdict.reason: Every cited location is present and matches the finding. crdt-tree.ts:195-199 reads `attrs.rowHeights` through a bare `Number(...)` with no range check, immediately adjacent to the diff's new `normalizeListLevel` clamp (crdt-tree.ts:244-250) that exists for exactly this trust boundary; the live reader repeats it at yorkie-doc-store.ts:453-455. table-layout.ts:244-252 adopts the value as a row minimum and applies only a floor (MIN_ROW_HEIGHT, lines 237-242) — a grep of packages/docs/src finds no MAX_ROW_HEIGHT or any page-count cap. pagination.ts:122-146 then loops `while (consumed < rowHeight)` with fragHeight bounded above by contentHeight (lines 130-134), calling startNewPage() (line 125) each iteration; paginateLayout (line 48) and startNewPage (63-73) impose no page limit, so rowHeight=1e12 yields ~1e9 iterations each allocating a page. The persistence path is unguarded too: the docs content validator only checks `Array.isArray(td.columnWidths)` and `Array.isArray(td.rows)` (docs-content.controller.ts:444-454) and never inspects tableData.rowHeights, and docs-tree.ts:158-162 serializes it verbatim into the tree attribute. No guard exists at any layer, so I have nothing to refute with; a write-scoped collaborator or API key can store a payload that hangs/OOMs every other reader and the PDF/CLI export.

finding.summary: Point-of-use clamp missing at the table-cell copy of the exact geometry sink the change hardened in the body layout
finding.evidence: The change normalizes the body list indent (`layout.ts:497`, `LIST_INDENT_PX * (normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel) + 1)`) with the rationale "a poisoned level multiplied into the indent is a NaN/Infinity marginLeft that blanks the block". The byte-identical expression for list items *inside table cells* is left raw: `table-layout.ts:93` computes `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` and folds it into `marginLeft` (line 101), from which `layoutBlock`/`applyAlignment`/row heights derive the whole table's and therefore the page's geometry. The same is true of every remaining raw reader: `doc-canvas.ts:599`, `paint-layout.ts:198`, `table-renderer.ts:524`, `peer-cursor.ts:254` and `:392`. Vector: any `listLevel` that is non-finite or far out of band and reaches a Block without passing `treeNodeToBlock`/`YorkieDocStore.treeNodeToBlock` (the two boundaries this change clamps) yields NaN or ~1e9-px geometry for every reader of that document, i.e. the same "blank the rendered document for every other reader" impact the change exists to prevent. I could not complete the chain to a concrete unclamped entry point for the docs *table* path — the CRDT boundaries (crdt-tree.ts:249, yorkie-doc-store.ts:501), the clipboard parser (clipboard.ts:348-351, finite-checked + clamped) and the backend read (`readDocsRoot` → docs `crdt-tree`) all clamp now — so confidence is low; the finding is that the defense now *reads* as complete (`docs/design/docs/docs.md`: "The raw readers clamp again at the point of use"; `list-level.ts:39-40`: "the raw readers call normalizeListLevel at the point of use") while five of them do not, which is the state in which the next non-CRDT entry point becomes exploitable silently.

verdict.reason: The finding claims table-layout.ts (and four other readers) multiply a raw `block.listLevel` into geometry without the `normalizeListLevel` clamp. The repository shows the opposite: `packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:95-98` computes `LIST_INDENT_PX * (normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel) + 1)` for the table-cell list indent, with an explicit comment (lines 92-94) citing the same NaN/Infinity marginLeft rationale as the body layout, and imports the helper at line 3. Every other reader the finding names as raw also clamps: doc-canvas.ts:603, paint-layout.ts:200, table-renderer.ts:529, peer-cursor.ts:257 and :396 (imports at doc-canvas.ts:2, paint-layout.ts:3, table-renderer.ts:5, peer-cursor.ts:3), plus pdf-painter.ts:370/:593 and markdown.ts:145. The quoted line numbers are a few lines off from the real expressions, and the real expressions are clamped. With the point-of-use clamps present, there is no unclamped geometry sink and no NaN/1e9-px denial-of-rendering vector, so nothing blocking under the security rubric.
